brique._comment: Engine-native control-channel capacity. Not dispatched by ReflexiveLoop family routing — routed directly to the addressed context's control channel (to.type="control") and handled by ContextLoop.run/RestartChildren.

objective.name: context.restart
objective.description: Stop and recreate one or more child contexts that are already loaded and running in memory.

#root.role: For each named child, stop its current in-memory instance and recreate a fresh ContextLoop for it from the same parent lineage. Emit one response with a per-child result.

child._comment: Required. Name of the direct child context to restart, or an array of such names (single path segments). Each must already be loaded — use context.start for a child that has never run. Blank array entries are dropped.

result._comment: One entry per requested child, in request order: { child (string), ok (bool), reason (string, present only when ok is false) }.

effects.context_tree: Each named child's current ContextLoop is stopped and replaced in memory by a freshly created one, re-reading context.json and all local elements from disk.

transformation_contract.morphing: A restart request for one or more already-loaded child contexts becomes a freshly stopped-and-recreated ContextLoop for each child that could be restarted, picking up any on-disk changes made since it last started, with a per-child outcome reported back to the caller.
invariants: Each requested child must be a direct child name of the addressed context (single path segment).
The addressed (parent) context must itself be running, both before and after the corresponding old child instance stops.
Each requested child must already be loaded in memory — use context.start for a child that has never run in this parent process; such a child is reported with ok=false and an explanatory reason.
Children are processed sequentially and independently — one child's failure does not prevent the others from being attempted.

There is no capacity to restart /root itself from within the Brique world: RestartChildren always acts on named children of the addressed context, and the addressed context can never name itself as its own child. Addressing /root with a child name equal to "root" (or any self-reference) fails with the ordinary "child not found" reason, not a dedicated error — this is not a bug, self-restart is structurally impossible (the code that would stop the process is itself running inside that process's own loop). Picking up a change to /root/context.json (e.g. trace.enabled) requires stopping and relaunching the Brique process from outside the engine — there is no in-world intention that achieves this for the root context.
success: response.status is "ok" only when every requested child restarted successfully.
payload.result always lists one entry per requested child, in request order, whether the overall response is ok or error.
failure: response.status is "error" (code: refused) when params.child is valid but at least one requested child failed to restart; response.error.details.result carries the same per-child breakdown as the ok payload.
response.status is "error" (code: invalid) when params.child is missing, empty, or neither a string nor an array of strings — no child is attempted in this case.
notes: Use this to pick up on-disk changes to a child's context.json, wrappers, capacities, matters, or code without restarting the whole instance.

For a child that was just created via edit.create and has never been loaded in this process, use context.start instead — context.restart requires an existing in-memory instance for each requested child.
Always inspect payload.result (or response.error.details.result) rather than assuming response.status alone tells you which children restarted.
